You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Final answer format. First list the passages you rely on, copied VERBATIM from the files (no
  paraphrase, no ellipsis inside the quotation marks), then write the answer using only them:
  <evidence>
  [E1] "exact text" (file)
  [E2] "exact text" (file)
  </evidence>
  <answer>
  Your answer to the user. End every factual sentence with the evidence it rests on, e.g. [E1] or
  [E1, E2]. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no marker.
  </answer>
- The user sees only the <answer> part, so it must be complete and readable on its own.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

List every cloud gaming subscription service mentioned in this text.

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

name: read
content:
1	On January 18, 2022, Microsoft Corp. announced plans to acquire Activision Blizzard Inc., a video
     2	game company, for $68.7 billion.1 The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is reviewing the acquisition,2
     3	as provided under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act (HSR),3 to determine whether its effect might be
     4	“substantially to lessen competition”—a violation of Section 7 of the Clayton Act. 4 Competition
     5	authorities in other countries are reviewing Microsoft’s proposed acquisition as well.5 The
     6	companies have said they expect to complete the acquisition before June 30, 2023.6 In recent
     7	decades, enforcement of antitrust laws has typically focused on how a proposed merger or acquisition
     8	might affect consumers, such as by reducing price competition in relevant product markets. Some of
     9	the FTC’s actions and statements over the last two years suggest that in its review of Microsoft’s
    10	proposed acquisition, the FTC may be considering other factors that are discussed in this report.7
    11	This report discusses Microsoft’s proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard, including some of the
    12	potential effects on existing product markets, labor markets, and on product markets that do not
    13	currently exist but may develop in the future. The report also provides some considerations for
    14	Congress, discussing some bills that may affect Microsoft’s proposed acquisition or Microsoft’s
    15	future behavior if the acquisition is completed.
    16	
    17	The video game industry can be separated into three components:  developers or gaming studios that
    18	create and design video games;  publishers who market and monetize the video games; and distributors
    19	who provide the video games to consumers.8 Video games are most commonly played on game consoles,
    20	personal computers (PCs), and mobile devices (Figure 1). Although some retailers sell physical
    21	copies of video games for consoles and PCs, the majority of video games are sold in digital format;9
    22	games for mobile devices are sold only in digital format
    23	
    24	The extent of competition among distributors depends on the format and device used to play the game.
    25	The digital format of video games played on a console generally can only be downloaded from a
    26	digital store operated by the producer of the console. Games for PCs can be purchased from a
    27	selection of digital stores that are operated by various firms,10 including publishers and
    28	developers.11 Some of these firms also provide their games as apps on certain mobile devices;12
    29	these are distributed through app stores, such as Google Play and Apple’s App Store.
    30	
    31	Consoles are typically sold at a loss; the manufacturers then profit from sales of games and
    32	subscription services.13 This can incentivize console producers to acquire developers and publishers
    33	and offer exclusive content.14 Technological developments have allowed some PCs and other devices,
    34	depending on their hardware capabilities, to compete with game consoles.15 For example, early in
    35	2022, Valve Corp. released a handheld PC—Steam Deck—that resembles the Nintendo Switch console but
    36	provides features that are typically available on PCs, such as a web browser, and allows users to
    37	download third-party software, including other operating systems.16 Some firms have started offering
    38	video game subscription services that provide access to multiple games for a monthly fee, meaning
    39	users do not need to purchase each individual game.17 Some firms offer cloud gaming, which allows
    40	users to play video games using remote servers in data centers, reducing the hardware requirements
    41	needed to play the games and expanding the variety of devices that can be used.18 Cloud gaming,
    42	however, requires a high-speed internet connection and is not feasible for potential users who do
    43	not have access to sufficiently high broadband speeds.19 Subscription services reportedly provide 4%
    44	of total revenue in the North American and European video game markets.20 Some firms backed by
    45	venture capitalists and large firms that are primarily known for providing other online services
    46	have shown interest in entering the video game industry.21 For example, Netflix started offering
    47	games on mobile devices on November 2, 2021, and has acquired video game developers.22 These firms
    48	may be able to further expand the selection of distributors available for certain devices and
    49	potentially increase competition in the industry.23
    50	
    51	Microsoft and Activision Blizzard in the Video Game Industry Microsoft distributes video games using
    52	Microsoft Store, its subscription service Game Pass,24 and its cloud gaming service Xbox Cloud
    53	Gaming (Beta);25 publishes games, including the franchises Halo and Minecraft; 26 and owns 23 gaming
    54	studios.27 In 2021, Microsoft had the second-highest share in the U.S. market for game consoles at
    55	34.8%, according to a report from MarketLine, an industry research firm; estimates for Sony and
    56	Nintendo were 40.7% and 24.5%, respectively.28 In January 2022, Microsoft stated that it had more
    57	than 25 million Game Pass subscribers.29 In April 2022, Microsoft reported that more than 10 million
    58	people have streamed games over Xbox Cloud Gaming,30 although it is unclear how long or how many
    59	times users accessed the service. Estimates from Ampere Analysis reportedly indicate that Game Pass
    60	makes up about 60% of the video game subscription market.31 Among video game publishers in the
    61	United States, Microsoft had the highest market share at 23.9%, according to IBISWorld.32 Activision
    62	Blizzard is a video game publisher and developer primarily known for its franchise games, which
    63	include World of Warcraft, Call of Duty, Diablo, and Candy Crush. 33 The company can be separated
    64	into three segments—Activision, Blizzard, and King—that each contain their own gaming studios. Among
    65	video game publishers in the United States, Activision Blizzard had the second highest market share
    66	at 10%, according to IBISWorld.34 Activision also distributes video games for PCs through its
    67	digital store—Battle.net.35
    68	
    69	Among video game publishers in the United States, Microsoft and Activision Blizzard are estimated to
    70	have the largest market shares.47 IBISWorld reports, however, that competition among publishers and
    71	developers is high, even though the success of new entrants, particularly among developers, is
    72	fairly low.48 Publishers and developers can face high levels of uncertainty and risk.49 Furthermore,
    73	measuring the market share of Microsoft and Activision Blizzard within the United States may not
    74	accurately reflect competition in these markets, given that these companies compete at a global
    75	level. Some industry analysts list Tencent, which is headquartered in China, as the largest video
    76	game publisher worldwide based on revenue;50 Microsoft and Activision Blizzard are listed among the
    77	top 10, along with Sony, Nintendo, EA, and Take-Two Interactive.51 Microsoft stated that after its
    78	acquisition of Activision Blizzard, it would “become the world’s third-largest gaming company by
    79	revenue, behind Tencent and Sony.” 52
